own_solution.law: Snell's law gives sin(theta_r)=sin(40 degrees)/1.8. Side reflections preserve the axial velocity component, so t=nL/(c cos(theta_r)).
assumptions: The end faces are perpendicular to the rod axis.
The nondispersive glass has pulse speed c/1.8.
The extension answers additionally require a straight continuation with the same refractive index as the rod; the added sentences do not specify this.

T51AF.regime: Total internal reflection persists for surrounding refractive index below n cos(theta_r)=1.68132; all three listed values satisfy this.

TD2A3.regime: Total internal reflection persists for surrounding refractive index below 1.68132; all three listed values satisfy this.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: T2524 and TB902 specify a glass coupler without its refractive index or alignment, whereas the certified answers require a straight extension made of the same n=1.8 glass.
defect_reasons.other: The authors incorrectly identify L tan(theta_r)/d as the literal number of zigzag legs and give q*ell/c as an outside-regime reference time even though q is the surrounding liquid's index, not the glass index.

counterexamples.description: An aligned 1.3 m nondispersive glass extension with index 1.5 and perpendicular interfaces gives approximately 20.04 ns, whereas an otherwise identical extension with index 1.8 gives 21.1977 ns; both satisfy the description 'glass coupler'.

For diameter 2.5 cm, L tan(theta_r)/d is approximately 30.585, which cannot be the literal number of legs; the central entry produces an initial half-width traversal and generally a final partial traversal.

At surrounding index q=1.9, any ray portion reflected back into the glass still propagates at c/1.8, while transmitted light follows a different path in the liquid; replacing the glass propagation time by q*ell/c does not describe either complete trajectory.

notes: The base relations and base numerical answer are correct. Under the additional same-glass, aligned-extension assumption, all three certified extension answers are correctly rounded. The disconnected sentences and the stated in-regime K answers are correct. Diameter independence is also correct: each segment has axial projection equal to its length times cos(theta_r), including partial segments, so the total path is L/cos(theta_r). The cancellation expression simplifies correctly, but its literal leg-count interpretation is inaccurate. Relative to pass 1, I withdraw rendering_not_minimal because pass 2 explicitly identifies T97AD and TACC7 as numeral-free controls and does not claim they preserve the number and unit; the actual minimal_pair_with links preserve 1.3 m. The coupler ambiguity remains unresolved because 'same glass' appears only in the authors' explanation, not in the problem or added sentences. No external information was accessed.
